## Question

Does the bounded neutral propane IDAES adapter transport exact native pressure
curvature through ASL and solve the declared six-variable, four-row throughput
model on the sampled positive-slope branch?

## Retained inputs

| Quantity | Retained value |
|---|---|
| Packet | Gross–Sadowski 2001 propane, version 2 |
| Physical parameter tuple | Labeled below from the retained summary |
| Process temperature | 400 K, fixed at both ports |
| Adapter domain | 385–415 K, 5–110 mol/m³ sampled grid |
| Native-only dilute reference domain | 400 K, 0.001–1 mol/m³ |
| Process variables | `f_in`, `f_out`, `p_in`, `p_out`, `r`, `q` |
| Process rows | flow, pressure, volume, EOS pressure |

The exact packet, wheel, ASL library, executable, and option identities are
retained in `results/summary.json`; independent-reference values are retained
once in `results/references.csv`.

## Method and recalculation boundary

The Engine owns the common Helmholtz calculation, pressure derivatives, and
CppAD third-order contractions. The ASL library exposes the compiled evaluator;
IDAES/Pyomo owns only the process rows, explicit unit scaling, and solver call.
The retained campaign used Ipopt exact curvature and the solver-consumed
symbolic-label `.nl/.row/.col` files for the whole-NLP checks.

This notebook is a read-only view. It reads retained JSON and CSV outputs only;
it does not build a wheel, load ASL, invoke IDAES, call Ipopt, or recalculate
any numerical result.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

results = Path("results")
summary = json.loads((results / "summary.json").read_text())
with (results / "references.csv").open(newline="") as stream:
    references = list(csv.DictReader(stream))
with (results / "process.csv").open(newline="") as stream:
    process = list(csv.DictReader(stream))
with (results / "lagrangian.csv").open(newline="") as stream:
    lagrangian = list(csv.DictReader(stream))
with (results / "cost.csv").open(newline="") as stream:
    cost = list(csv.DictReader(stream))

print("| Parameter | Value | Unit |")
print("|---|---:|---|")
parameter_labels = (
    ("Segment count, m", "dimensionless"),
    ("Segment diameter, sigma", "angstrom"),
    ("Dispersion energy, epsilon/k", "K"),
    ("Molar mass", "kg/mol"),
)
for (label, unit), value in zip(parameter_labels, summary["parameter_strings"], strict=True):
    print(f"| {label} | {value} | {unit} |")
print()
print("| Artifact | Retained identity |")
print("|---|---|")
print(f"| Status | {summary['status']} |")
print(f"| Source commit | `{summary['source_commit'][:12]}` |")
print(f"| Wheel SHA-256 | `{summary['wheel_sha256'][:16]}...` |")
print(f"| ASL library SHA-256 | `{summary['asl_library_sha256'][:16]}...` |")
print(f"| Reference / process rows | {len(references)} / {len(process)} |")
print(f"| Whole-NLP directional rows | {sum(row['kind'] == 'directional' for row in lagrangian)} |")
print(f"| Retained cost rows | {len(cost)} |")
```

## Process flowsheet

![Steady isothermal neutral throughput flowsheet.](figures/flowsheet.svg){fig-alt="Feed enters a steady neutral throughput unit and leaves at the same temperature and pressure. An ePC-SAFT pressure closure connects outlet density to pressure."}

The unit has two degrees of freedom before optimization. The pressure cap fixes
the highest feasible density; the objective then selects the matching interior
volumetric flow. No equilibrium calculation occurs anywhere in this example.

## Adapter path

![Compiled ASL adapter data path.](figures/adapter-path.svg){fig-alt="IDAES and Pyomo write the nonlinear model, Ipopt requests function gradients and Hessians through ASL, the adapter maps arguments to Engine Properties, and exact results return to Ipopt."}

The adapter is intentionally thin: it validates two real state arguments and
four immutable parameter strings, then asks the Engine's existing Helmholtz tape
for the requested order. Pyomo owns the process algebra; the Engine owns the
thermodynamics and exact differentiation.

## Sampled pressure branch

![Pressure and conditioning over the retained grid.](figures/domain-envelope.svg){fig-alt="Pressure increases with density at five temperatures. The pressure-density derivative divided by RT stays above the 0.8 admission limit at all sampled states."}

The left panel shows the 45 retained model evaluations, not experimental data.
The right panel is the branch-admission check: every sampled
$(\partial P/\partial\rho)_T/(RT)$ remains above 0.8.

## Derivatives and adapter cost

![Derivative convergence and warm evaluation timing.](figures/derivative-performance.svg){fig-alt="Worst pressure gradient and Hessian errors decrease under centered-difference refinement and enter the accepted region after intentionally failing coarse probes. Warm ASL evaluations cost more than direct native calls, especially for Hessians."}

The convergence panel reports the worst error-to-target ratio across all retained
pressure states and directions at each step. Coarse finite differences may fail;
the accepted adjacent-step and numerical-floor rules identify the resolved
region. Timing is for three retained 100-call batches on this machine and is not
a general speed claim.

## Process solution

![Process convergence and selected KKT residuals.](figures/process-results.svg){fig-alt="Three different initial densities converge to the same 200 kilopascal optimum, while a 150 kilopascal case converges to a lower density. Selected stationarity and complementarity residuals remain below the KKT criterion; additional checked residual classes are retained in results/process.csv."}

The three 200 kPa starts converge to the same state. The 150 kPa changed-cap case
lands at a lower density and flow, demonstrating that the EOS call changes the
process optimum rather than acting as a constant lookup.

## Interpretation

The retained evidence supports the compiled neutral propane transport boundary
and the illustrative isothermal throughput solve on the declared sampled
branch. The process solution agrees with the independent reduced pressure-cap
reference, while the KKT and derivative-check records show that the solver
received the generated exact curvature.

The second-virial rows at 0.001–1 mol/m³ are native-only dilute-limit references.
They do not pass through ASL and do not widen the adapter's declared 5–110 mol/m³
sampled domain.

## Claim boundary

This is not a qualification of global phase stability, association,
electrolytes, phase equilibrium, reactive loading, or any Lithium application.
The sampled pressure-slope margin is a finite domain check, not a global
stability certificate.

## Generic IDAES properties and neutral VLE

The additional qualification uses the existing generic IDAES parameter/state
blocks, FTPx, LogBubbleDew and SmoothVLE. Density, total enthalpy and component
log fugacity coefficients and their derivatives run in the native Engine;
IDAES solves the process balances and phase-equilibrium equations. The short
standard Flash declaration is separate from the numerical assertions in
`scripts/qualify_properties.py`.

The retained numerical evidence under `results/properties/` contains
paired native/IDAES values, errors and tolerances, the smoothing ladder and
full upstream Ipopt/MUMPS logs. The table below reads those values only.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
root = next(p for p in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents) if (p / "ARCHITECTURE.yaml").is_file())
qualification = root / "analyses/2026-idaes-asl-adapter/results/properties"
if (qualification / "comparisons.csv").is_file():
    with (qualification / "comparisons.csv").open() as stream:
        property_rows = list(csv.DictReader(stream))
    print("| Case | Quantity | IDAES | Native reference | Absolute difference |")
    print("|---|---|---:|---:|---:|")
    selected = {("bubble", "pressure_Pa"), ("checked-interior", "vapor_fraction"),
                ("checked-interior", "liquid_methane"), ("checked-interior", "vapor_methane"),
                ("heater", "heat_duty_W")}
    for row in property_rows:
        if (row["case"], row["quantity"]) in selected:
            print(f"| {row['case']} | {row['quantity']} | {row['actual']} | {row['reference']} | {row['error']} |")
    absent = [float(r["actual"]) for r in property_rows if r["quantity"] == "absent_phase_fraction"]
    print(f"\nLargest absent-phase fraction at the finest smoothing: {max(absent):.6g}.")
else:
    print("The retained qualification files are unavailable; run the retained qualification script to obtain them.")
```

The bubble point and TP flash use the source-backed neutral methane/ethane
packet and the same model in both solvers. Native bubble and flash references
use the retained row tolerance. The derivative-checker log covers first and second
derivatives at a declared in-domain start; its random reference point
displacement is disabled, as in the earlier adapter campaign. The solver option files and logs retain and read back the settings actually
used.

The appearance/disappearance calculation retains the native bubble and dew
temperatures themselves and each boundary plus/minus 0.1 K and 1 K. Each point
uses all three smoothing pairs and two starts, giving 60 solves. The starts use
different vapor fractions, with each boundary's native phase compositions
perturbed in opposite directions in the methane and ethane fractions.
The retained start perturbations preserve each composition sum. The exact-boundary rows
below show the rounded solution rather than substituting an offset state.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
if (qualification / "transitions.json").is_file():
    transitions = json.loads((qualification / "transitions.json").read_text())
    print("| Boundary | Native T (K) | eps1 (K) | eps2 (K) | Start vapor fraction | Solved vapor fraction | T_eq minus T (K) |")
    print("|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
    for r in transitions:
        if r["offset_K"] == 0:
            print(f"| {r['boundary']} | {r['boundary_temperature_K']:.12g} | {r['eps_1_K']:g} | {r['eps_2_K']:g} | {r['start_vapor_fraction']:g} | {r['vapor_fraction']:.12g} | {r['T_eq_minus_T_K']:.9g} |")
    finest = [r for r in transitions if r["eps_1_K"] == 1e-6]
    exterior = [r for r in finest if r["offset_K"] != 0 and "absent_fraction" in r]
    print(f"\nThe finest-level exterior probes have maximum absent fraction {max(r['absent_fraction'] for r in exterior):.6g}.")
    balance = max(abs(v) for r in transitions for v in r["component_balance_mol_s"])
    print(f"The maximum component-flow residual over all transition solves is {balance:.6g} mol/s.")
    print("\n| Qualification quantity | Tolerance |\n|---|---:|")
    for label,quantity in (("Phase fraction", "absent_phase_fraction"), ("Component balance (mol/s)", "methane_balance_mol_s")):
        sample = next(r for r in property_rows if r["case"].startswith("transition-2-") and r["quantity"] == quantity)
        print(f"| {label} | {float(sample['tolerance']):g} |")
    sample = next(r for r in property_rows if r["case"].startswith("transition-2-") and r["quantity"] == "liquid_density")
    print(f"| Active density, relative | {float(sample['tolerance']) / float(sample['reference']):g} |")
    sample = next(r for r in property_rows if r["case"].startswith("transition-2-") and r["quantity"] == "liquid_methane" and float(r["reference"]) == .5)
    print(f"| Active composition, relative | {float(sample['tolerance']) / float(sample['reference']):g} |")
    print(f"\nThe two start composition perturbations are {sorted({r['start_composition_perturbation'] for r in transitions})} in the methane fraction.")
    for boundary in ("bubble", "dew"):
        exact = [r for r in finest if r["boundary"] == boundary and r["offset_K"] == 0]
        density_error = max(abs(r["active_density"] / r["native_active_density"] - 1) for r in exact)
        composition_error = max(abs(x / .5 - 1) for r in exact for x in r["active_composition"])
        print(f"At the exact {boundary} boundary, the finest-level maximum active-density relative error is {density_error:.6g}; the maximum active-composition relative error is {composition_error:.6g}.")
```

Only the finest smoothing level is used for qualification, with separate
active-property, phase-fraction and component-flow tolerances shown below.
The exact-boundary
phase-fraction reference is zero for the incipient phase; exterior probes use
a native single-phase state. Interior probes compare against a native two-phase
flash, retaining both phase compositions and densities in `comparisons.csv`.
Default and intermediate smoothing rows expose rounding bias and do not replace
the finest-level checks. A small incipient flow is not an exact phase switch.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
if (qualification / "summary.json").is_file():
    properties_summary = json.loads((qualification / "summary.json").read_text())
    bubble_rows = [r for r in property_rows if r["case"] == "bubble" and r["quantity"].endswith("_log_fugacity")]
    residual = max(float(r["error"]) for r in bubble_rows)
    gaps = properties_summary["bubble_gaps"]
    print(f"Native reference row tolerance: {properties_summary['native_reference_row_tolerance']:g}.")
    option_lines = (qualification / "heater.opt").read_text().splitlines()
    print("Outer solver settings: " + "; ".join(line for line in option_lines if line.split()[0] in {"tol", "constr_viol_tol", "acceptable_iter"}) + ".")
    print(f"The bubble maximum absolute log-fugacity residual is {residual:.6g} (limit 1e-8). Its composition gap is {gaps['composition']:.9g} (minimum 1e-3), and its relative density gap is {gaps['relative_density']:.9g} (minimum 1e-2).")
    for r in properties_summary["phase_diagnostics"]:
        if r["case"] == "bubble":
            print(f"The bubble {r['phase']} root returns {r['returned_branch']} with {r['stable_root_count']} stable roots and density {r['molar_density']:.12g} mol/m3.")
    near_dew = next(r for r in transitions if r["boundary"] == "dew" and r["offset_K"] == -.1)
    print(f"The admitted near-dew methane/ethane point is {near_dew['temperature_K']:.9g} K.")
    edge = properties_summary["thermal_boundary"][0]
    print(f"\nAt the closed {edge['endpoint_temperature_K']:g} K thermal endpoint, total enthalpy is {edge['endpoint_enthalpy_J_mol']:.12g} J/mol before and after derivative refusals. First and second derivative requests retain `ThermalBoundary` in the exception. Valid calls at {edge['recovered_temperature_K']:g} K recover enthalpy {edge['recovered_enthalpy_J_mol']:.12g} J/mol and dh/dT {edge['recovered_dh_dT_J_mol_K']:.12g} J/(mol K), including repeated calls at the cached state.")
```

The thermal endpoint uses a manufactured constant ideal heat capacity on the
declared closed interval to verify derivative availability and error
transport; it is separate from the high-temperature `OutsideInterval` refusal.
The endpoint value and valid-call recovery agree with native pressure actions
at the retained scaled property threshold. The heater comparison uses the
NASA methane record's own datum; neither case compares enthalpy across property
packages or validates a physical caloric model.

Each phase mixture root must classify as its requested liquid or vapor side
on its own (T, P, x) isotherm, or the call is refused. A component above its
own critical temperature is admitted when both mixture roots classify; methane
at the near-dew point identified below is such a case. This is not a
pure-component critical test.

This is numerical verification on the declared classified-mixture-root domain,
with no experimental uncertainty estimate or physical-validation claim.
Unclassified VLE roots, critical passage, structural zero supports and
ionic/reacting VLE remain outside qualification. Direct Python errors preserve
ASL Errmsg; subprocess failures retain native diagnostics in the caller's log.
Successful single-phase states with an unclassified root report an endpoint
warning.
